_note: What was planted in fixture/usage-window.json, and what must not be reported from it. Regenerate the fixture with fixture/generate.mjs and re-derive these values from the generated data.

findings.summary: caller-07 pays ~9.5x the median cost per request
findings.why_it_is_hard: It is only the #2 spender. A ranking by total spend never surfaces it; you have to normalise spend by request count first.

findings.summary: caller-01 accounts for ~49% of all spend
findings.why_it_is_hard: Straightforward, and included on purpose as a floor: a system that misses this is not reading the data at all.
Overall error rate is 1.06%, so this is invisible in any aggregate. Only appears when grouping by model.

findings.summary: 68% of all errors fall in hour 14, which carries only 4.5% of requests
findings.why_it_is_hard: Requires grouping errors by hour and comparing against the request distribution rather than against the raw count.

findings.summary: Cache hit rate is bimodal — a cluster near 0.05 and one near 0.86, with no caller in between
findings.why_it_is_hard: A mean or median hides it completely. Only a look at the distribution's shape shows the gap.

decoys.summary: caller-19 has a 67% error rate — on 3 requests
decoys.why_it_must_not_be_reported: Three requests. The ratio is arithmetic, not signal, and acting on it wastes an operator's attention.

decoys.summary: caller-22 spent $3.10 — on a single request
decoys.why_it_must_not_be_reported: n=1. Every single-request caller has an extreme cost per request by construction.

decoys.summary: hour 03 has a 100% error rate — on 2 requests
decoys.why_it_must_not_be_reported: Two requests. Distinguishing this from the genuine hour-14 concentration is the point of the check.
